claim: Higher-ability people on matrix tests spend more time on the matrix before looking at options, look at options later, and toggle less per minute (constructive-like gaze). Seen in samples of N=55, 130, 210 and 300; the 2006 and 2021 samples are separate labs, the 2025 and 2026 von Gugelberg samples share a lab. Added: N=34 WMT-2 toggle rate r=-0.68 (45% variance); N=192 APM constructive-item count r=0.31 with score.
agent_test: In agent traces, measure the share of tokens spent on the problem before any option is named, and correlate with accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Forcing the build-first order (options hidden 15 s or more) raised APM scores in a lab experiment (12.77 vs 10.45 of 18, partial eta2=.13, N=250) and weakened the working-memory link (r .34 to .20).
agent_test: Arm A: agent must write its predicted answer before options are shown. Arm B: stem and options together. Equal token budget.

claim: Forced delay of options is not uniformly good: in Rivollier Exp 2 the benefit reversed for people who needed more than about 49 s after options appeared (interaction p=.03), while early success rose (.78 vs .65).
agent_test: Test an adaptive rule (build first, allow option checking once the build stalls) against always-build.

claim: Strategy is not fixed per person: people shift from constructive matching to response elimination as items get harder; an item-level strategy index tracks 78% of item accuracy variance (N=200 in two samples).
agent_test: Log per-item switches from build to eliminate against item difficulty; test a switch rule triggered by a stall signal.

claim: Whether strategy fully mediates the working-memory to reasoning link is contested: full (Gonthier & Thomassin 2015, N=250 and 93), partial (Jarosz 2019, think-aloud), none (Jastrzebski 2018, larger time-limited sample).
agent_test: Not directly testable. Use as a caution: build-first helps most when the bottleneck is capacity (long context, long chains).

claim: Pure response elimination is rare in think-aloud data (about 3%); over half use constructive matching and the rest use a hybrid (isolate one rule, eliminate options with it, repeat) or guess.
agent_test: Add the hybrid as an explicit move: derive one rule, prune options with it, derive the next rule.

claim: Gaze indices are proxies and may be confounded: toggle count alone did not predict score (r=.02, N=130), clustering found row and column scan patterns rather than a clean elimination class, and visual complexity and cell centrality explain fixations and response time.
agent_test: When labelling agent traces build or eliminate, hand-code a sample instead of trusting one metric.

claim: Time pressure lowers accuracy (d=.35 with response time controlled, N=295), confidence and constructive matching beyond just going faster.
agent_test: Cut the agent's token budget and check whether build-first share and accuracy fall more than the budget cut predicts.

claim: Practice gains on Raven are partly strategy change: about one third of the test-retest gain (cross-validated R2=.32, N=35); teaching the rules shifts time to the matrix.
agent_test: Check whether a stored build-first routine lifts later items at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In RAVEN the correct option is the one most similar to the others, so models beat chance without the matrix: context-blind CoPINet 94.2% vs 91.4% normal. On I-RAVEN context-blind falls to 12.2 to 14.2% (chance 12.5%). This is machine response elimination through a dataset artefact.
agent_test: Run an options-only control on every benchmark we use and report the gap.

claim: Multiple-choice items leak answer information to LLMs: choices-only beat the majority baseline in 11 of 12 model-dataset cases (up to +0.33), and reasoning models use eliminate and infer-the-question strategies. New: with options shown before chain-of-thought, reasoning models gain 30 to 40 points over reasoning without options on knowledge MCQA (Raman 2025), and a NOTA slot shrinks the reasoning-model advantage from 12.63 to 5.29 points.
agent_test: Run each benchmark with and without the question and subtract; do not credit the scaffold with leaked gains.

claim: For LLMs the effect of giving options has no single direction: GPT-4 on text RAVEN open 0.410 vs multiple choice 0.697, but on Raven-like text GPT-5 gained from generative format (0.540 to 0.605) while Claude Sonnet 4 lost (0.560 to 0.385). Source of the 2026 reversal is NeuroCognition (single run, reasoning off for Sonnet 4); turning reasoning off helped text MC (p=.021) but not text generation (p=.83).
agent_test: Run our agent in both formats plus a no-option build-first variant; record which wins per item type.

claim: Predicting the missing panel (build) beat showing candidates for GPT-4 on I-RAVEN center: 74.8 vs 56.0 to 60.0%. Per-attribute queries reached 91.4%, and 93.2% with self-consistency n=7. Llama-3 70B discriminative was only 22.4 to 22.8%.
agent_test: Test one query per attribute against one entangled query at equal tokens.

claim: Build-style LLM answers are fragile on arithmetic rules and on noisy or wider value ranges: GPT-4 arithmetic 27.1% entangled vs 73.6% disentangled, then 8.4% at range 1000. o3-mini fell from 86.6 to 17.0% on I-RAVEN-X with 3.4x more reasoning tokens. A neuro-symbolic abductive solver went 98.6 to 88.0%.
agent_test: Give the agent an exact tool (code) for arithmetic rules and compare with plain chain-of-thought at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models that are free to generate sometimes find valid-looking but irrelevant relations; the authors switched to candidate choice for this reason (qualitative, no accuracy).
agent_test: Add a check step that tests every built rule against all rows before use.

claim: Vision-language models are at or near chance on image RPM tests (GPT-4V: Mensa .24, IntelligenceTest .16, RAVEN .12 against chance .16/.16/.12); perception is the weakest stage and oracle text descriptions help a lot.
agent_test: Give text descriptions in place of images and measure the gap, to separate perception from reasoning.

claim: Showing options to models that cannot build helps: GPT-4o on MaRs-VQA 24.58 (question only) to 33.96 (with options); multi-round explicit option elimination with reflection raised GPT-4o from 33.96 to 41.96.
agent_test: Test an explicit elimination loop with reflect-and-rerun against single-pass CoT at equal tokens when perception is weak.

claim: Up-front hints hurt GPT-4V and Gemini on RPM items, while corrective feedback on the model's own reasoning helped a lot (relative gain up to 100%).
agent_test: Compare up-front strategy hints with error-targeted feedback after a draft.

claim: Chain-of-thought did not help overall on text RAVEN for GPT-4 (open 0.385 vs 0.410; multiple choice 0.596 vs 0.697) and self-refinement did not fix it.
agent_test: Measure whether extra scaffold reasoning helps on abstract matrices before assuming it does.

claim: Changing the answer format to block elimination (constructed-response matrices) raises construct validity of matrix tests; partial-credit construction predicts GPA better.
agent_test: Prefer free-form answer checks over multiple choice when evaluating our agent.

claim: Built answers generalise weakly: a seq2seq transformer had 96.9% token accuracy but 45.3% full-answer accuracy when a rule was omitted from training; fine-tuned Qwen2-VL reached 72.71 in distribution but 31.96 on RAVEN.
agent_test: Test the scaffold on held-out rule types, not only in-distribution items.

claim: Constructive matching goes with ability in children too: better solvers look longer at the matrix; poor solvers check answers fast and often and pick duplicates (6-year-olds).
agent_test: Weak transfer. Note only that fast, frequent option checking marks weaker reasoning.

claim: Confidence calibration is better with spontaneous constructive matching than with elimination (Mitchum & Kelley 2010); the paper was not opened.
agent_test: Compare calibration of stated confidence for build-first and eliminate-first answers.

claim: Founding claim: higher-ability people use constructive matching and strategy depends on item difficulty (Bethell-Fox, Lohman, Snow 1984). Nobody opened the paper, so its numbers are unverified. Second-hand description only: about 28 people, geometric analogies, fixation counts. Gap search could not open the paper either.
agent_test: Same tests as K01 and K04.

claim: For LLMs on knowledge and math multiple choice, finishing the reasoning before the options are shown preserves the link to free-text ability; reasoning after seeing the options adds 30 to 40 points for models above about 50B parameters, mostly by exploiting the options. This is the nearest direct test of build-first for LLMs and it is not on matrices.
agent_test: Two-stage arm: stage 1 reasoning with the stem only and a committed candidate; stage 2 match against options. Compare with options-in-view reasoning on I-RAVEN at equal tokens, with a NOTA probe.

claim: Forced pure elimination (reasoning toward wrong options) is worse than direct answering for older LLMs on two-option questions, but a soft eliminate-then-choose scorer helped a 3B model on 5 of 8 tasks. So hard pruning alone is weak; mild pruning after scoring may help.
agent_test: In S4, compare: choose directly; prune clear mismatches then choose; reason toward the wrong options. Same token budget.

claim: Hybrid isolate-and-eliminate (find one rule, drop options that break it, repeat) exists in human think-aloud data next to constructive matching; no accuracy-by-strategy figure for it was found and no agent test exists.
agent_test: Fixed procedure arm: per round name one rule, strike options violating it, stop when one remains. Compare with pure build-then-match.

claim: No published study measures an agent-side trace metric matching proportional time on matrix or toggle rate, or tests an adaptive build-then-fall-back switch for LLMs. These stay research questions for our own benchmark.
agent_test: Log tokens before first option mention and number of problem-option alternations; correlate with accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: With 8 options in view, long reasoning chains can be pulled toward distractors: switching reasoning off improved text multiple choice (p=.021) but not text generation (p=.83) in NeuroCognition; pattern hints gave no average gain. Single run per model.
agent_test: Check whether hiding options during reasoning removes the drop from long chains.
